battle.name: 固石洞之戰
battle.brief: 紹興三年四月，岳飛率師入虔州，圍剿彭友、李滿等經營三四年、橫跨十餘州的虔吉變民軍。彭友被擒，眾退保雩都山區固石洞，四面環水、僅一條路可入。岳飛移師瑞金，張憲、王貴迂迴兩翼，佯攻數日耗其滾木礌石，再以三百敢死士奪隘合圍。卡面十字弩未見於宋軍，於此役只作封隘射擊。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方，是南宋朝廷與江西虔州、吉州一帶的變民軍。變民軍並非國家軍隊，而是建炎四年（1130年）以來在虔州（治贛縣，今江西贛州市）與吉州（今江西吉安市）兩州境內先後起事、由數十萬民眾自發聯合而成的武裝，首領多為民間豪強與地方武人，其中吉州的彭友、李滿自號「十大王」，虔州的陳顙、羅閑十各領一部；數百處山寨依山深谷林相互策應，縱橫轉戰於虔、吉、循、梅、潮、惠、英、韶、南雄、南安、建昌、汀州諸州。南宋一方則是剛渡江建國、北方故土未復的朝廷：軍令出自行在臨安的樞密院，江西一路的安撫司、制置司與各州知州、縣令分掌民政與緝捕，岳飛以神武副軍都統制領兵入虔，節制虔吉一線的官軍。所謂官軍，是禁軍、廂軍與各路勤王兵、弓箭手的混合體，裝備以長弓、弩、長槍、大刀為主，糧秣由州縣供應。兩造的差別不只在大義與名分，更在補給：官軍有糧、有州縣、有後方，變民軍有地利、有熟路的嚮導、有數百處可輪替的山寨。這場仗本質上是南宋開國頭十年在腹地收拾內亂的一次軍事行動，卻發生於宋金戰爭尚未結束的背景下，北方戰線吃緊，南疆安撫成了次要方向上的急務。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the Southern Song court and the rebel communities of the prefecture of Qian and the prefecture of Ji in Jiangxi. The rebel force was not a national army but a body of arms raised on its own since the fourth year of Jianyan (1130), when, in the territory of Qian (seat at Ganzhou, present-day Ganzhou City, Jiangxi) and Ji (present-day Ji'an City, Jiangxi), tens of thousands of the common people joined together in revolt against the oppression of the local officials and the depredations of the imperial troops. The insurgents in Ji were led by Peng You and Li Man, who styled themselves the Ten Great Kings, while in Qian the leaders were Chen Yong and Luo Xianshi, each leading a band of his own. They occupied hundreds of strongholds, every one of them set in defensible country, supported one another through the deep mountains and dense forests, and fought their way across the prefectures of Qian, Ji, Xun, Mei, Chao, Hui, Ying, Shao, Nanxiong, Nan'an, Jianchang and Ting. The Song side was a court that had only just crossed the river and founded itself, with its old territories in the north still lost. Orders came from the Bureau of Military Affairs at the temporary capital Lin'an; in Jiangxi, the pacification and control commissions, together with the prefects of the various prefectures and the magistrates of the counties, divided between civil administration and the policing of the countryside, while Yue Fei entered Qian at the head of his troops as deputy commander of the Divine Might army and took command of the imperial forces along the Qian-Ji line. What those imperial troops were meant was a mixture of palace guards, provincial levies and troops mustered from the various circuits together with their bowmen, armed above all with long bows, crossbows, long spears and broadswords, and fed by grain supplied from the prefectures and counties. The difference between the two sides lay not only in the cause and the legitimacy but in the supply: the imperial army had grain, had prefectures and counties, had a rear; the rebels had the ground, had guides who knew the paths, and had hundreds of sites from which they could rotate. This campaign was in essence a military operation by which the new Southern Song state tidied up unrest in its own interior during the first decade of its existence, and it unfolded against the background of a war against the Jin that was still unfinished: the northern front was consuming the court's attention, and pacifying the southern marches became an urgent task on a secondary front.
people: 岳飛是全場唯一留下姓名的指揮官。紹興三年（1133年）四月，他以神武副軍都統制的身分奉命率軍抵達虔州，這時他還不到三十歲，卻已在曹成、張益、李成等一連串平叛與北伐中建立起「岳家軍」的作戰名聲。彭友等退入雩都山區據險待戰，岳飛沒有立刻強攻，而是先遣使詔諭，結果變民軍寧戰不降，反而出山迎戰，官軍初戰即擒彭友，眾部受創退保固石洞。真正決定戰局的是接下來的部署：岳飛移師瑞金，分派統領官張憲、王貴各率一軍迂迴兩翼，自己親率一路正面進兵，三路約期合圍。抵達固石洞下，他見山高阻險、四面環水，只有一條路可入，便以馬軍重鎧列陣山下，伐木造天橋，佯攻數日，誘使守寨者把滾木礌石用盡；然後派三百敢死士登山突破隘口，山下同時鳴鼓呼噪造聲勢。變民軍不辨官軍多寡，慌亂中墜崖身死者甚眾，下山奔逃者盡被包圍，李滿等首領相繼被俘。變民軍一方除了彭友、李滿，還有虔州的陳顙、羅閑十等名號首領，各據一寨、互為聲援，其中數人是在後續掃清各處山寨時先後落網或逃散。此外還有一批沒留下姓名的角色：山寨中負責放滾木礌石、掘陷坑、斷樹伐木的雜役與獵戶，以及隨義軍作戰的地方團練。岳飛在虔州並未濫殺，而是以招撫安民作為收治之法，這一點後來成為他與朝中主張峻烈剿辦者分歧所在。
peopleEn: Yue Fei is the only commander in this affair who is named in the record. In the fourth month of the third year of Shaoxing (1133) he reached Qian at the head of his troops as deputy commander of the Divine Might army; he was not yet thirty, but he had already built the fighting reputation of what came to be known as the Yue family army in a long series of actions against Cao Cheng, Zhang Yi, Li Cheng and others. When Peng You and the rest withdrew into the mountains of Yudu to hold defensible ground, Yue Fei did not strike at once but first sent an envoy with a proclamation, and the rebels chose to fight rather than surrender and came out of the hills to meet the imperial troops; the first engagement produced the capture of Peng You and losses that drove the survivors back to the cave of Gushi. What really decided the battle was the deployment that followed: Yue Fei moved his command to Ruijin, gave the commanders Zhang Xian and Wang Gui one force each to turn the two wings, and led one column himself in the frontal approach, the three columns to converge at an appointed hour. Arriving beneath the cave he saw that the hill was high and the approach steep, that water surrounded it on four sides and that only one path led in, so he drew up the armoured horse in line at the foot of the mountain, cut timber for a trestle bridge, and made a feint of assault for several days, inducing the garrison to expend its rolling logs and stones; then he sent three hundred picked men up the mountain to break through the pass while drums were beaten and shouts raised below to make noise. The rebels, unable to tell how many imperial soldiers there were, panicked in the confusion and many were killed falling from the cliff, those who fled down the slope were surrounded, and leaders such as Li Man were taken prisoner. On the rebel side there were besides Peng You and Li Man such named chiefs as Chen Yong and Luo Xianshi of Qian, each holding his own stockade and answering one another's signals, some of whom were caught or dispersed as the remaining strongholds were cleared in turn. There are also roles that left no names: the porters, hunters and woodcutters in the stockades who rolled the logs, dug pits and felled the trees, and the local militia who fought alongside the insurgents. At Qian, Yue Fei did not let the killing run; he made the pacification of the people and the recruitment of the surrendered his method of closing out the affair, and this would later mark the difference between him and those at court who argued for the harshest possible suppression.
kits: 這張卡上的十字弩，出自十二世紀初的英格蘭—歐洲體系，是把弓弦扣在弩機上、以絞筋或踏板張弦的歐洲式弩，與歐洲弩手裝備的弩矢、護臂、皮兜及備件同出一套體系。在固石洞之戰的戰場上，這種形制並沒有原樣出現：宋軍的弩不是歐洲式，而是自成一系的蹶張弩、神臂弓與牀子弩，靠弓力大、射程遠、破甲力強見長，安裝與張弦須多人合力，攜行要拆件分載，顯然不是可以單兵帶上山的機關。但弩的戰術位置在兩邊是一致的：弩手不與人面對面搏鬥，只在固定陣位上遠射掩護，掩護攻城、堵隘、封路與居高臨下的射擊；在固石洞這種四面環水、僅一條通道的地形，弩兵最合適的位置正是兩翼迂回部隊占據的兩側山脊與主道兩旁的岩壁，用交叉火力把唯一的通道封死，等於用器械代替城牆。與此同時，弩的弱點在這場戰役裏暴露無遺：裝填遲緩，射後數十息才能再射，一旦守方把滾木礌石用盡、封死道路被突破，弩手便再沒有第二次射擊的機會，只能退入後方掩體。攻方實際倚仗的裝備清單是這樣的：正面的重鎧馬軍與步軍持長槍、矟槍與朴刀、麻札刀，配大盾與拒馬；弓手以長弓、角弓覆蓋射界，另有少量神臂弓壓制岩壁上的守軍；後勤靠馬匹、騾車輸送糧秣與柴薪，糧道自虔州方向沿山道遞送；強攻器械包括伐造的天橋、隨軍攜帶的繩梯與飛樓，以及為封路而砍伐的巨木。用弩對付這樣的守備本可行，問題在於弩兵太少、太慢，一旦被拖入近身格鬥便毫無作用。
kitsEn: The crossbow on this card belongs to the England-Europe system of the early twelfth century: a European crossbow in which the string is held in a trigger and the bow is spanned by a windlass or a stirrup, belonging to the same outfit as the bolts, the forearm bracer, the pouch and the spare parts carried by a European crossbowman. In the field at the battle of Gushi that form did not appear. The Song crossbow was not European but a family of its own, the zhuzhang crossbow, the Shenbin bow and the bed crossbow, distinguished by great draw, long reach and heavy armour-piercing power; installing and spanning them required several men together, and they were carried in pieces for transport, so they were plainly not machines a man could take up a mountain. Yet the tactical position of the crossbow was the same on both sides. The crossbowman did not fight at close quarters but covered fixed positions with long-range fire, and his work was to cover assaults, block passes, seal roads and shoot from the heights. In terrain like Gushi, ringed by water on four sides with a single approach, the ideal place for the crossbow was exactly the ridges held by the two flanking columns and the rock walls beside the main path, where crossing fire sealed the only entrance, so that the instrument did the work of a wall. The weakness of the crossbow at the same time was laid bare by this campaign: reloading is slow, and it takes tens of breaths before a second shot can be loosed, so once the defenders had spent their rolling logs and stones and the blocked path had been broken, the crossbowmen would never get a second volley and could only fall back behind cover. The list of equipment on which the assault actually relied ran thus: the frontal armoured horse and the foot carried long spears, halberds, broadswords and knives, with big shields and caltrops; bowmen with long and composite bows covered the field of fire, with a few Shenbin bows to pin the defenders on the cliff; for the rear, horses and mule carts carried grain, firewood and timber, the supply line running up the mountain paths from the direction of Qian; and for the assault itself, the trestle bridge cut on the spot, rope ladders and flying towers carried with the column, and the great trees felled to seal the road. The crossbow could have served against such a defence; the difficulty was that there were too few crossbowmen and they were too slow, and once drawn into a fight at close quarters they were useless.
tactics: 這場戰役的戰術可以拆成三段：先在虔州城郊以詔諭試探，等到彭友被擒、眾部退保山區，再把整個作戰重心搬進雩都山區；第三段是攻固石洞的合圍作戰。過程中有幾個要點。第一是官軍主動放棄正面強攻，改用三路迂迴：岳飛移師瑞金，等於先把指揮部與後勤基地往南挪，使兩翼部隊得以瑞金為支點同時向西北方向夾擊；張憲、王貴各領一軍走山路迂迴，岳飛自率一路從正面推進，三路約期合圍，山區裏的路線選擇因此比正面火力更要緊。第二是佯攻與消耗：重鎧馬軍列陣山下，伐木造天橋，日日進逼，卻不真正投入攻梯，誘使守寨的變民軍把滾木礌石、落石與弓矢傾瀉到陣前，等他們把防禦物資用盡。第三是破口：三百敢死士在夜色與鼓噪掩護下登山直取隘口，山下同時鳴鼓呼噪，把守方注意力釘在正面，使變民軍無法判斷官軍到底有多少。第四是斷糧與封路：四面環水、只有一條路可入的地形，意味著守方的糧秣全靠這條路；兩翼合圍一旦完成，就等於切斷了唯一的補給線，山寨不必被強攻便會自行崩解。第五是速戰：山區四月多雨，糧道越長消耗越大，遠程運糧的馬隊在狹窄山道上難以展開，官軍沒有曠日持久的餘地，因此從抵達到破寨只以數日計。變民軍也不是沒有應對：他們據險待戰、互相支援、寨寨相望，本可輪番騷擾與消耗以拖垮遠來的官軍，但彭友被俘造成的指揮斷裂，加上唯一通道被封死，使這套原本有效的防禦失去支點。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this campaign fall into three stages: first the probing of the rebel positions in the open before Qian with proclamations and envoys, then, once Peng You had been taken and the survivors driven back into the hills, the centre of gravity of the operation was moved into the mountains of Yudu, and the third stage was the encirclement assault on the cave of Gushi. Several points stand out. First, the imperial army deliberately gave up the frontal assault and turned to a movement in three columns. By shifting his command to Ruijin, Yue Fei moved his headquarters and his supply base southward, so that the flanking columns could pivot on Ruijin and strike simultaneously from the north-west; Zhang Xian and Wang Gui led their forces by mountain paths to turn the two wings while Yue Fei pressed in from the front with one column, the three to converge at an appointed moment, and in the mountains the choice of route mattered more than frontal firepower. Second, the feint and the exhaustion of the defenders: the armoured horse stood in line below the mountain, trees were cut for a trestle bridge, the line was advanced day after day, yet no real escalade was attempted, in order to make the garrison pour its rolling logs, its stones and its arrows onto the ground in front of the formation until its stores of defensive material were spent. Third, the breach: three hundred picked men went up the mountain in the covering of darkness and noise to seize the pass, while drums beat and shouts rose below, fixing the defenders' attention on the front so that they could not judge how many imperial soldiers there were. Fourth, the cutting of supply and the sealing of the road: a place ringed by water on four sides with only one path leading in meant the defenders' food came entirely along that path, and once the two flanks had closed, the only supply line was cut, so the stockade would collapse of its own accord without needing to be stormed. Fifth, speed: the hills in the fourth month are wet, the longer the supply line the more it consumed, and a train of pack animals could not deploy on narrow mountain tracks, so the imperial army had no room for a protracted contest, and from arrival to the breach of the cave took only a matter of days. The rebels were not without answers either: they held defensible ground, supported one another and watched one another's stockades, and they could have worn down a distant imperial army by rotating harassment and attrition; but the break in command caused by the capture of Peng You, together with the sealing of the single path, deprived that defence of its footing.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾處。起事時間在建炎四年（1130年），到紹興三年（1133年）四月平定，歷時三四年。變民軍的規模以「數十萬」民眾響應、「扎寨數百處」記載，活動範圍遍及虔、吉、循、梅、潮、惠、英、韶、南雄、南安、建昌、汀州等十餘州。作戰時間是紹興三年四月，岳飛四月抵達虔州，同月破固石洞。官軍的部署為三路：張憲、王貴各率一軍迂迴兩翼，岳飛親率一路正面進兵，約期合圍；破隘的突擊兵力是三百敢死士；佯攻歷時數日。地形上，固石洞山高阻險、四面環水，只有一條路可入，這一點決定了整場戰役的樣子。距離上，以今公路里程計，虔州治贛縣至雩都、瑞金各約一百數十公里，全軍需走兩三日山道才能進抵山區。器械方面，弩的有效射程一般在一百五十至三百公尺上下，遠不及長弓的上限，但精度高、破甲力強；神臂弓一類的強弓射程更遠，卻必須安裝就位才能使用，拆裝需時日，在這種速戰速決的條件下只能用在少數幾個固定陣位。戰果沒有留下確切數字：彭友、李滿等首領被俘，變民軍多傷亡，各山寨被各個擊破，虔州、吉州平定。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are concentrated in a few places. The rising began in the fourth year of Jianyan (1130) and was ended in the fourth month of the third year of Shaoxing (1133), a span of three or four years. The scale of the insurgents is recorded as tens of thousands of the people joining in and as hundreds of sites being stockaded, with their operations extending across a dozen or more prefectures: Qian, Ji, Xun, Mei, Chao, Hui, Ying, Shao, Nanxiong, Nan'an, Jianchang and Ting. The fighting took place in the fourth month of 1133: Yue Fei reached Qian in that month and broke the cave of Gushi in the same month. The imperial deployment was in three columns, Zhang Xian and Wang Gui with one force each turning the two wings and Yue Fei leading one column in the frontal approach, converging at an appointed hour; the shock troops committed to the pass were three hundred picked men; the feint lasted several days. As to the ground, the cave of Gushi was high, steep and ringed by water, with one path leading in, and that single fact determined the shape of the whole engagement. As to distance, by present-day road mileage it is a hundred-odd kilometres from the seat of Qian at Ganzhou to Yudu and to Ruijin alike, and the column needed two or three days on the mountain tracks before it reached the hills. As to the weapons, the effective range of a crossbow is generally from a hundred and fifty to three hundred metres, well short of what the long bow can reach, but with better accuracy and heavier armour-piercing effect; bows of the Shenbin class shoot further still, yet must be set up before use and take time to shift, and under conditions demanding a quick decision they could only be employed at a few fixed positions. No exact figures survive for the results: Peng You and Li Man were taken prisoner, the rebels suffered many casualties, the stockades were broken one after another, and Qian and Ji were pacified.
cause: 起事的第一推力是建炎四年（1130年）湖南鐘相、楊幺反宋。鐘相、楊幺在洞庭湖水鄉起事，響應者眾，朝廷調兵圍剿，江南西路一帶的官府胥吏與過境官軍趁亂加徵、抄掠，民間怨憤很快在山區找到出口。虔州與吉州地處江西、廣東、福建三省之交，山深谷險，州縣控制力本來就弱，虔州屬縣虔化、瑞金一帶的山民與客籍百姓在鐘相、楊幺之後接踵而起，數十萬民眾聯合，抗拒官府壓迫與官軍抄掠。到1129至1133年間，虔州變民首領陳顙、羅閑十與吉州變民首領彭友、李滿分頭立寨，號「十大王」，在數百處山寨之間相互策應，屢次擊敗前來鎮壓的州兵與募兵，聲勢愈盛，遂令虔、吉各州屢次上書請朝廷派大軍。第二層原因是朝廷自身的政治邏輯：南宋立國未久，中原故土盡失，北方對金作戰是頭等大事，腹地叛亂就必須迅速壓平，否則州縣不能徵發、漕運不能暢通，江南的財政與兵源都會受影響。於是在外線戰事吃緊的同時，朝廷仍抽得出神武軍一系的精兵入虔，把平叛交給最能打的軍隊。第三層原因在宋金戰爭的大背景下：紹興二年、三年朝廷正忙著整頓江淮與襄漢的防線，腹地若再久拖，會被視為內部失序，士氣與號令都難以維持，這正是岳飛受命入虔的真正背景。
causeEn: The first impulse behind the rising was the revolt of Zhong Xiang and Yang Yao in Hunan in the fourth year of Jianyan (1130). The two rose in the lake country of Dongting and drew a wide response, and while the court moved troops to surround them, the clerks of the administration and the imperial soldiers passing through took the opportunity to raise levies and to plunder, and the anger of the people found an outlet in the hills with great speed. Qian and Ji lie where Jiangxi, Guangdong and Fujian meet; the mountains are deep, the valleys steep, and the reach of the prefectures and counties was weak to begin with. Among the hill folk and the itinerant households of the Qian counties of Qianhua and Ruijin, the same grievance that had flared after Zhong Xiang and Yang Yao flared again, tens of thousands of people joining in to resist the oppression of the officials and the depredations of the soldiers. Between 1129 and 1133 the Qian leaders Chen Yong and Luo Xianshi and the Ji leaders Peng You and Li Man raised their stockades separately, took the title of the Ten Great Kings, and supported one another from hundreds of strongholds, beating back the prefectural troops and the recruited levies that came against them again and again, until the prefectures of Qian and Ji petitioned the court again and again for a major army. A second cause lies in the court's own political logic: the Southern Song had been founded only a short while, the Central Plain was lost beyond the river, the war against the Jin in the north was the first matter of the state, and rebellion in the interior had to be crushed quickly, or the prefectures could not levy, the grain convoys could not run, and the revenue and the manpower of the south would all suffer. So even while the external front was hard pressed, the court could still detach the picked troops of the Divine Might army to Qian and hand the suppression to the best fighting force it had. A third cause lies within the setting of the war against the Jin: in the second and third years of Shaoxing the court was busy restoring its defences along the river and in the Xiang-Han region, and a prolonged domestic outbreak would be read as disorder at the centre, undermining both the morale and the authority of the orders, and that is the true background against which Yue Fei was ordered into Qian.
impact: 固石洞之戰的直接結果是虔州、吉州平定，橫跨十餘州的變民軍被連根拔起：核心山寨攻破，首領成擒，餘部在失去統一指揮之下被各個擊破。這一戰也把岳飛推到南宋中期最耀眼的位置上。平定虔吉之後，他名聲大振，隨即被調往湖南，參與平定洞庭湖水軍，隨後移師荊湖北路，收復襄陽六郡，第四次北伐的序幕由此拉開；可以說，江西這場平叛是他由「平叛將軍」轉為「大將」的一塊跳板。第二層影響是對南宋初期地方治理的刺激：變民軍能在虔吉立寨數百處、橫行三四年，說明建炎以來州縣武備空虛、胥吏剝削與糧運阻塞的問題已積累到失控邊緣；岳飛在虔州止殺安民、以招撫為先的做法，與朝廷原本的峻烈剿辦主張相左，事後看，虔吉一帶的生產與徵發很快恢復，沒有像某些反覆起事的地區那樣長期空虛。第三層影響在戰術思想上：這一役留下了「依山據險、三路合圍、佯攻消耗、破隘殲敵」的完整樣本，宋軍後續在荊湖、襄漢地區對山地抗禦的戰鬥，思路與此同源。第四層影響是南宋正規軍對地方武力的壓倒性展示：變民軍可以靠地利與數十萬人眾久據山寨，但只要指揮統一、補給跟得上、封住唯一通道，數百處山寨便會在數月內連鎖瓦解，這一點對後來平定五龍山寨與鄱陽湖區諸役都有參照價值。
impactEn: The direct result of the battle of Gushi was the pacification of Qian and Ji and the uprooting of an insurgent movement that had stretched across a dozen prefectures: the central strongholds were stormed, the leaders taken, and the remaining bands were broken one by one in the absence of any central command. The victory also carried Yue Fei to the most prominent place of his generation in the middle Southern Song. After Qian and Ji were settled his name was suddenly known far beyond the south, and he was moved to Hunan to take part in the reduction of the Dongting lake fleet, then transferred to the northern circuit of Jinghu, where he recovered the six prefectures of Xiangyang, and the fourth northern expedition began to unfold from there: the pacification of the rebels in Jiangxi was the stepping stone that turned a general of pacification into a great commander. A second effect was on the working of local government in the early Southern Song. The rebels had been able to raise hundreds of stockades in Qian and Ji and to hold the country for three or four years, which showed that the county military had been hollowed out since Jianyan and that the exactions of the clerks and the jamming of the grain convoys had accumulated to the point of breakdown. Yue Fei's refusal to give way to mass killing at Qian, and his preference for pacification and recruitment, ran against the court's original policy of ruthless suppression; in the event, production and levies in Qian and Ji recovered quickly and did not lie empty for long as they did in some regions where rebellion broke out again and again. A third effect lay in tactical thinking: this campaign left a complete model of holding difficult ground, closing in with three columns, wearing the enemy out by feint, and breaking the pass to destroy, and the Song operations against mountain defences in Jinghu and Xiangyang in the following years were conceived along the same lines. A fourth effect was the demonstration of the overwhelming superiority of the regular Song army over local armed bands: rebels might hold a mountain for years on the strength of the ground and a host of tens of thousands, but as long as the command was unified, the supply kept up and the single road was sealed, hundreds of stockades would collapse in a matter of weeks, and this had its value for the later reduction of the Wulong strongholds and the Poyang lake country.
result: 紹興三年四月，固石洞被攻破。彭友在退入雩都山區之前於虔州一帶被官軍所擒，眾部受創後退保固石洞；岳飛移師瑞金，以張憲、王貴兩軍迂迴兩翼、自領一路正面進兵，三路約期合圍，重鎧馬軍列陣山下、伐木造天橋連日佯攻，把守寨變民軍的滾木礌石耗盡；三百敢死士登山奪隘，山下鳴鼓呼噪，變民軍不辨官軍多寡，慌亂中墜崖身死者甚眾，下山奔逃者盡被包圍，李滿等首領被俘。其後其餘山寨被岳飛率軍各個擊破，虔州、吉州平定，綿延三四年的虔吉變民軍至此瓦解。收尾上，岳飛沒有遵照宋高宗以峻烈手段剿辦的詔令大肆屠戮，而是安撫江西百姓、招撫散眾，只將首領與核心骨幹收押問罪。戰後岳飛的兵馬得以脫離山區，奉調轉赴湖南，投入對洞庭湖水軍的進攻，南宋在腹心的最大一處內部動亂亦告一段落。需要說明的是，關於這場戰役的兵力、斬獲與俘虜數字，現存記載極為簡略，能確定的只有上述過程、指揮配置與結果；至於各寨守軍規模、官軍傷亡數目，以及自1130年起事至平定之間各次戰鬥的具體經過，史料多付闕如，本篇只就《固石洞之戰》一條所載的框架作實錄，不作推補。
resultEn: In the fourth month of Shaoxing the third year, the cave of Gushi was taken. Peng You had been captured by the imperial troops in the region of Qian before the retreat into the hills of Yudu, and the survivors, mauled, fell back on the cave of Gushi. Yue Fei shifted his command to Ruijin, gave Zhang Xian and Wang Gui a force each to turn the two wings and led one column in the frontal approach himself, the three converging at an appointed hour; the armoured horse stood in line at the foot of the mountain, timber was cut for a trestle bridge and the feint was pressed for several days, wearing out the rebels' rolling logs and stones; three hundred picked men went up the mountain to seize the pass, and with drums beating and shouts raised below, the rebels, unable to tell how many imperial soldiers there were, panicked and many were killed falling from the cliff, those who fled down the slope were surrounded, and leaders such as Li Man were taken prisoner. The remaining stockades were then broken one by one by the troops Yue Fei led, Qian and Ji were pacified, and the Qian-Ji rising that had run for three or four years came to an end. In the closing of the affair, Yue Fei did not carry out the mass killing ordered by Emperor Gaozong on the harshest terms but pacified the people of Jiangxi and recruited those who came in, confining punishment to the leaders and the hard core. After the campaign his troops were able to leave the hills and were transferred to Hunan for the attack on the Dongting lake fleet, and the largest single outbreak of internal disorder in the Southern Song heartland was closed out. It should be said that the numbers of troops, of kills and of prisoners for this campaign survive in the record only in the most fragmentary form; what can be established is the course of operations, the command dispositions and the outcome set out above. As for the size of the garrison in each stockade, the losses on the imperial side, and the detailed course of the several engagements fought between the rising of 1130 and its suppression, the sources are largely silent, and this account confines itself to the framework contained in the single record of the battle of Gushi without filling the gaps by conjecture.
